title: Mallard Duck Movement
text:
This site explores 83,279 GPS and Argos locations collected from 52 tagged mallards (Anas platyrhynchos) between 2007 and 2017. Most fixes come from birds tagged near Radolfzell on Lake Constance—a large lake on the border of Germany, Switzerland, and Austria—and over 99% of recorded locations stay close to the lake. Still, a handful of individuals range much farther across Central and Eastern Europe, reaching as far north as 53.9°N and as far east as 23.6°E.
Across the year, recorded activity peaks in late summer and autumn (especially September), when movement speeds also tend to be slightly higher than in winter and spring. Use the Map and Seasons pages in the navigation bar above to see where each duck traveled and how speed distributions change from month to month.
